9
The space probe Rosetta was designed to investigate a comet. The probe consisted of an orbiter
and a lander. The orbiter had a mass of 170 kg and the lander had a mass of 100 kg. When the
two parts separated, the lander was pushed towards the surface of the comet so that its change
in velocity towards the comet was 3.0 m s–1.
orbiter
mass 170 kg
lander
mass 100 kg
3.0 m s–1
Assume that the orbiter and lander were an isolated system.
The orbiter moved away from the comet during the separation.
What was the change in the speed of the orbiter?
A
1.8 m s–1
B
2.3 m s–1
C
3.0 m s–1
D
5.1 m s–1

hints: Notice the orbiter mass $170 \text{ kg}$, lander mass $100 \text{ kg}$, and lander velocity change $3.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ toward the comet.
For the isolated orbiter-lander system total momentum is conserved, so the two momentum changes are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
Set $m_{orbiter} \times \Delta v_{orbiter} = m_{lander} \times \Delta v_{lander}$ and solve for the orbiter change using the given masses.
walkthrough: Identify the isolated system: orbiter plus lander, so total momentum does not change during separation.
State the rule: increase in momentum of the lander toward the comet equals decrease in momentum of the orbiter, so $m_L \Delta v_L = m_O \Delta v_O$ in magnitude.
Rearrange for the orbiter: $\Delta v_O = (m_L / m_O) \times \Delta v_L$.
Substitute values with units: $\Delta v_O = (100 \text{ kg} / 170 \text{ kg}) \times 3.0 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 300/170 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate and check: $\Delta v_O \approx 1.76 \text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 1.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away from the comet. This is option A.

A.explanation: Magnitudes of momentum change are equal, so $170 \times \Delta v = 100 \times 3.0$ gives $\Delta v \approx 1.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: This is not obtained from momentum conservation with masses $100 \text{ kg}$ and $170 \text{ kg}$ and $3.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: The speed changes are not equal because the masses are different, so momentum $m\Delta v$ must be balanced.

D.explanation: This adds the effects as $3.0 \times 170/100$, which inverts the mass ratio and violates equal opposite momentum changes.
